area_summary: All game 2D (HUD, menus, message boxes, J2D screens, the dDlst_2D* raw quads, 2D JPA particles, the 2D J3D list) goes through one J2DOrthoGraph: the stack object `graf` that mDoGph_Painter builds every frame (m_Do_graphic.cpp:1572-1576, 1890-1891) and publishes as dComIfGp_getCurrentGrafPort() (the only other publisher is drawDvdCondition, the disc-error screen). Its viewport/bounds are the full EFB (0,0,640,480); its ortho box is the overscan box (-9,-21)-(650,503), written in source as setOrtho(-9,-21,659,524) = x,y,w,h. The compiler folded that into the .sdata2 pair 0x803F7D68=-9 / 0x803F7D6C=650 (x) and 0x803F7D60=-21 / 0x803F7D64=503 (y), so 659 2D units span 640 EFB px. **Best choke point:** J2DOrthoGraph::setOrtho (0x802CDD14), widening the box's x about its centre by F. Not C_MTXOrtho inside setPort: J2DPane clipping reads mOrtho through scissorBounds, and C_MTXOrtho/GXSetProjection are shared with the full-EFB passes. setOrtho has exactly 4 DOL callers, all `bl`s that can be hooked (Painter 0x8000B06C and 0x8000BA30, dOvlpFd2 0x80223CF4, drawDvdCondition 0x8003EADC), and no REL calls it. One ~0x50-byte T2 function covers every J2D screen, the dDlst_2D* quads, the 2D particles, and every `getCurrentGrafPort()->setPort()` re-issue (about 30 files). **Bypass census:** (1) about 14 passes have their own projection over the full EFB and are naturally full width, so they need no change: calcFade, motionBlure, drawDepth (DOF plus the letterbox bars), the alpha/spot passes, the pause-menu and game-over backdrop captures, the fade snapshots, dSnap's alpha clear, JUTFader (drawn under JFWDisplay::endGX's own 640x480 ortho), clearEfb, and the JUT debug overlays. (2) Four places do hard-coded maths that ties 2D units to EFB pixels with the vanilla box, and they break under compression: the cutscene wipe box 0x803F89B8, dOvlpFd4's 2Dt_Sp constants 0x803FB78C/0x803FB77C, the minimap's dMap_c::calcScissor, and the dead 2Dtact/2DCopy. The first two are cheap data rewrites. (3) Two places draw 2D in EFB pixels under their own ortho: the photo freeze-frame setUpRectangle (which shares the Painter's constants) and pictureDraw (private constants). (4) Four perspective draws in the 2D phase scale by g_HIO.mAspectRatio: dOvlpFd2's spinning snapshot, the two cloth backdrops and the file-select camera. That last class turns the choice of 3D knob into a hard constraint (open questions). Cheap: the setOrtho hook (or a data rewrite of 0x803F7D68/6C plus 0x803FB734/3C) and the wipe and Fd4 data rewrites. Moderately cheap: per-screen full-width escapes (J2DScreen::draw with a NULL graf, or two J2DFillBox side fills, a few bytes per site). Expensive: re-anchoring each HUD element and fixing each screen-pixel conversion (the HUD/menu/text-box agents' job).

items.assumption: The 2D design space is 640x480 with an overscan box: ortho x -9..650 (659 units) mapped onto the 640 px EFB viewport (J2DGrafContext bounds 0,0,640,480). 1 2D unit = 640/659 EFB px, centred at 2D x 320.5 = EFB px 320.
items.effect_native: Unfixed under the anamorphic model, every HUD element, menu, text box, title, map and 2D particle is stretched horizontally by F (4/3 at 16:9). With the hook, all of it is drawn unstretched in the centre 4:3 region (2D x 0..640 occupies the middle 1/F of the screen). After that, the full-screen items listed below must be expanded again and the HUD re-anchored (HUD agent).
items.anchor: centre (compression about 2D x = 320.5, the box centre = screen centre); y untouched
items.fix: T2 C hook (core owns the sites), hook_branchlink at all four bl sites 0x8000B06C, 0x8000BA30, 0x80223CF4, 0x8003EADC (all or none: if only the Painter's are hooked, Fd2's restore puts an uncompressed box back mid-frame for everything drawn after it in 2DXlu). typedef struct{f32 x0,y0,x1,y1;}WsBox; typedef void(*setortho_fn)(void*,const WsBox*,f32,f32); #define J2DOrthoGraph_setOrtho ((setortho_fn)0x802CDD14). void ws_set_ortho_hook(void* g,const WsBox* box,f32 far_,f32 near_){WsBox b=*box; f32 F=ws_ui_factor(); /* 1.0 unless WWWS magic ok && mode==2 && 1<=factor<=3 */ if(F!=1.0f){f32 c=0.5f*(b.x0+b.x1); b.x0=c+(b.x0-c)*F; b.x1=c+(b.x1-c)*F;} J2DOrthoGraph_setOrtho(g,&b,far_,near_);}. F=4/3 gives the box -118.833..759.833 (0xC2EDAAAB / 0x443DF555). mOrtho changes, so setPort (C_MTXOrtho+GXSetProjection) and scissorBounds (pane clipping, getWidthPower) both follow and stay consistent. The hook reads the factor on every call, so a mode change takes effect on the next frame. Cost: ~0x50 bytes of T2 and 4 DOLPatches entries. Zero-hook alternative (what the Gecko does): from C, at boot and on every WS op, write x0'/x1' into 0x803F7D68/0x803F7D6C and 0x803FB734/0x803FB73C (plain data, read by lfs every frame, no JIT issue). Side effect: setUpRectangle (photo freeze-frame) shares 0x803F7D60..6C and would be compressed too, see 2d-picto-capture. Prefer the hook. Rejected: hooking `bl C_MTXOrtho` in setPort (0x802CDCF0): pane scissors would mismatch, and it would also compress JUTFader, the JUT debug overlays and the J2DScreen NULL escape hatch.

items.fix: Two tools: (1) the Gecko trick: overwrite the `mr r4,r31` before the bl with `li r4,0` (0x38800000). J2DScreen then draws through its private 0..640 ortho: full width, ~3% larger than the -9..650 box, and the art is stretched. Caveat: that path leaves its own 0..640 projection current, so later raw dDlst_2D* items that don't call setPort draw wrongly. (2) Better: hook_branchlink the bl with ws_draw_screen_full(J2DScreen* s,f32 x,f32 y,J2DOrthoGraph* g), which saves g->mOrtho (+0xBC), restores the vanilla x box (-9,650), calls g->setPort() (0x802CDCB4), J2DScreen::draw(s,x,y,g), then restores the compressed box and calls setPort() again (~0x60 B, shared by all sites). For screens with centred art (game-over letters) the menus agent should prefer widening only the backdrop pane, per element. Whether to escape each screen is the screens agent's call.

items.dol: Copy: 0x8000AD8C bl GXSetTexCopySrc(320-152,180-104,304,208), GXSetTexCopyDst(152,104,fmt,GX_TRUE = 2:1 box downscale). setUpRectangle: 0x8000A6A8..B4 lfs 0x803F7D60/64/68/6C (shared with the Painter), C_MTXOrtho bl 0x8000A6C0. pictureDraw: viewport 0x80227A30 (0,0,640,480); private ortho constants 0x803FB81C=-21, 0x803FB820=503, 0x803FB824=-9, 0x803FB828=650 (loads 0x80227BA0..AC, used only here), C_MTXOrtho bl 0x80227BB8; quad = pane centre ±152 x ±104 (pane_no[] positions are in compressed 2D space).
items.assumption: The EFB, the viewfinder art and the photo quad all share the 4:3 pixel space
items.effect_native: Photos are copied from the anamorphic EFB (304 EFB px = 405 4:3-equivalent units, while the viewfinder now frames only 304 of them). The freeze-frame redraw (setUpRectangle's vanilla ortho) lands exactly on its source, so it looks right but is wider than the compressed viewfinder frame. With the data-rewrite variant of the choke point it would be compressed and squashed. The album pictureDraw places a vanilla-ortho quad at a compressed pane centre: the photo shows at correct proportions but 4/3 wider than its frame.
items.fix: The 2:1 box filter fixes the copy at 304x208→152x104 (the card format), so rect maths alone can't make it exact. Options: (1) default and cheapest: leave capture, setUpRectangle and pictureDraw vanilla (the setOrtho hook does that). Photos look correct and only the frame art mismatches the photo size; or put the whole picto-box screen on the NULL escape hatch, which stretches the frame art. (2) Crop: keep the capture, draw with texcoords limited to the centre 1/F (load a GX texture matrix s'=0.5+(s-0.5)/F for TEXCOORD0) at the compressed rect. This needs hooks at the C_MTXOrtho bls 0x8000A6C0 and 0x80227BB8 (widen the box like the choke) plus a texture-matrix setup. The photo then matches the viewfinder exactly but loses 25% horizontal resolution. (3) Capture 228x208→114x104: breaks the card format, rejected. The picture-evaluation (d_snap) subject checks are 3D-projection based (3D agent).
items.gecko: pictureDraw only: rewrites the GXSetViewport args at 0x80227A18/1C/20 (viewport x 79, w 480: compresses the photo into the centre). The freeze-frame is compressed via the shared 0x803F7D68/6C.

open_questions: The knob is a hard constraint between areas. widescreen-culling.md §9 counts 'g_HIO.mAspectRatio widens the stage-transition fade (d_ovlp_fade2.cpp:54)' as a benefit, but that is backwards. With the g_HIO knob, Fd2's snapshot quad (±320 at z=-420, fovy 60) covers only 77% of the EFB and of the screen, so every stage transition opens with a squashed image and side gaps. With the 4/3 literal 0x803FA998 (loaded only by preparation at 0x8017BE5C), Fd2 is seamless, but the name-scene camera (0x80230034) needs its own fix and the two cloths stay stretched. Pick one: (a) literal knob + name-scene fix, or (b) g_HIO knob + Fd2 hook at 0x80223A10. Decide with the door-transition live check.
Does the pause-menu cloth (scale 1.78) and the file-select cloth (1.27x0.93) overfill a 16:9 frustum under the g_HIO knob, or leave gaps? Only a live screenshot answers this.

Picture box: should photos match the viewfinder (crop with a texture matrix, losing 25% horizontal resolution) or keep the vanilla capture (correct proportions, wider than the frame art)? The 2:1 GXSetTexCopyDst box filter and the 152x104 card format rule out an exact capture.

Which J2D screens besides Ow_mask, game over, the opening, the telescope and the picture box have full-screen backdrop panes (menu fades in dMenu_* noteOpen/Close, place-name backdrop at dPlace_name_c::setScreen 0x8016103C, the save and option screens)? That list belongs to the menus/HUD agents; this area provides the two tools (ws_draw_screen_full / NULL graf, and ws_fill_sides).

RELs were not scanned in RELS.arc. In the decomp source no REL calls setOrtho or sets the graf port. d_a_movie_player is the only REL with its own 2D ortho; whether WW USA ever spawns it was not checked.
